en: So let's start with the most basic way of
working with Bun, using it as a runtime.
I got a TypeScript file here because as
mentioned, Bun can natively execute
TypeScript. Obviously it can also execute
JavaScript, but here it's a TypeScript file.
And in that file I'm using some TypeScript
features, having a type definition, a type
alias here,
using that alias here and then also here for
typing this parameter of this function.
And then I just execute that function, pass
my dummy object to it and console.log it.
Dummy example here, of course.
Now you can run bun run
and then that file, in my case demo.ts,
and execute that file with Bun and it'll
just, well, execute it so that you see the
output here.
Now, worth noting, as I mentioned before, is
that with modern Node, so in my case here,
for example, I have version 26. You may very
well already have a more recent version, but
with modern versions of Node, you can also
execute that file and it will work. So
that's not just a Bun feature anymore.
Still, it is also a Bun feature and using it
as a runtime is kind of the main thing
you'll probably do with Bun.
